newsitem.title: FRANCE: Andre shares jump, firm sees profit ahead.
newsitem.headline: Andre shares jump, firm sees profit ahead.

text.p: Investors drove up shares of Groupe Andre more than three percent on Monday in what traders said was recognition of the clean-up of the shoemaker's accounts after it reported a full-year net loss.
"The market appreciates the housekeeping" done by company chairman Jean-Claude Sarazin, one trader said.

By 1109 GMT, Andre's shares were up 3.29 percent at 399.0 francs. Earlier, it announced a net loss of 976 million francs for the year to end August 1996 against a loss of 35 million, on sales of 10.32 billion francs, down 0.6 percent on the previous year.
The firm, which took an exceptional charge of 887 million francs for 1995/96 of which 659 million was linked to restructuring, forecast a return to profit for 1996/97.
Sarazin is aiming to rid the company of its loss-making activities and revitalise its sales outlets.
The company said the financial year had begun under satisfactory conditions with sales up four percent in the first quarter on a like-for-like basis.
